name: Man-Carrying Cargo Drone (Improvised)
description: A cargo drone modified to carry a human passenger. This is exactly as dangerous as it sounds. Tier 1 ingenuity at its most desperate — an Arcturus Mule drone with the cargo bay stripped and a seat (or harness, or rope) installed. The drone's lift capacity barely handles an adult human, the battery life is halved, and the stability algorithms freak out because the payload keeps shifting. People ride these because the alternative is worse. The mortality rate is not tracked because no one wants to know.
range: 10 km (reduced from cargo spec due to weight)
cost: Φ50-100 per ride from operators, Φ2,000 to buy a modified unit
autonomy: Autonomous drone flight with manual override (joystick strapped to the frame)
common_usage: Desperate emergency transport, smuggling, accessing locations with no other approach, proving a point.
story_hooks: A meat drone operator has been running a clandestine air ambulance service in The Shelf, saving lives at the risk of their own
Someone straps a bomb to a meat drone and the entire improvised air transport network gets cracked down on — killing the ambulance service too
physical_description: A battered Arcturus Mule cargo drone, its matte gray composite hull scarred by impact marks and patched with mismatched industrial tape. The cargo bay has been gutted and replaced with a welded-steel seat frame bolted directly to the frame, fitted with frayed nylon straps and a single cracked safety harness that looks like it was salvaged from something else entirely. Exposed wiring and hastily-soldered battery connections run along the underside, still dripping residue from whatever adhesive holds them in place.
visual_prompt: battered gray cargo drone with human seat welded inside, exposed wiring, industrial tape patches, cracked safety harness, worn composite hull, rain-slicked metal, product photography, gritty cyberpunk, neo-noir, dark moody lighting, detailed wear and corrosion, desperate jury-rigged engineering, dark background
